inputs.sbc_source: Not disclosed as an expense line in the tanshin or yuho (J-GAAP filer). The only equity-linked remuneration is a Board Benefit Trust holding 132,200 shares (0.1% of issued) with a provision of 328m yen at 2026-06-30 -- immaterial, carried as an explicit 0% SBC row (SBC-zero market).
inputs.fy0_note: Metrics.csv labels fiscal years by the calendar year of the 31 March year-end: CSV FY2026 = year ended 2026-03-31 = company label 'FY2025'. FY0 here is the year ended 2026-03-31; projection Y1 is the year ending 2027-03-31 (company 'FY2026', the guided year).
inputs.share_count_basis: 134,800,000 issued less 1,310,767 treasury shares (incl. 132,200 held by the Board Benefit Trust) = 133,489,233 at 2026-06-30 (Q1 tanshin). No dilutive securities: the company does not present diluted EPS. Held FLAT: SBC is nil so there is no dilution to charge; the 10.5bn yen buyback running May 2026-Mar 2027 (~2.1m shares, ~1.5% of count) is real accretion the flat-count convention ignores -- conservative.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. 10-year JGB ~1.6% (Oct 2026) + Japan ERP 6.0% x beta 1.05 (semis-exposed specialty chemical) = cost of equity ~7.9%; debt is ~4% of EV at ~0.5% after tax, giving a WACC of ~7.6%. Rounded to 7.5% and held identical across scenarios: cyclicality and semis concentration are charged in the bear path, not stacked on the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside operating profit, so the lease cost is already in EBITDA. Finance leases are negligible (leased assets, net 118m yen). No lease principal deducted and no lease liability in net debt -- treatment (B) by default of the accounting standard, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated operating profit; non-controlling interests (3,949m yen book at 2026-06-30; 791m yen of FY0 profit, 1.6%) are deducted once in the equity bridge, not in the flows.
inputs.non_operating_assets: Investment securities 35,355m yen at 2026-06-30 (AFS cross-shareholdings at fair value plus equity-method affiliates at book). Their income (dividend income 1,578m, equity-method earnings 1,507m in FY0) sits below operating profit and is therefore outside the EBITDA-driven flows, so the asset goes into the bridge at 85% of carrying value (30,050m) to allow for tax on unrealised gains. Interest income (178m) is likewise below OP and is stripped from last_fcf per the owner-FCF identity; net debt is a small positive 9,134m so the cash pile is not double-counted.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 2: non-US operating company, adaptations file applied -- JPY WACC, J-GAAP leases, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule for cross-shareholdings, SBC-zero so house and street coincide and band_position is degenerate: treat it as n/a). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Working capital: trade receivables 100.2bn + inventories 78.1bn - trade payables 23.8bn = 154.5bn, 55% of revenue, so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is set at -20% of the revenue change rather than the full -55% because FY2025-26 absorbed only ~6% of a 28bn revenue increase (inventories fell while sales grew) and inventory is seasonal in agrochemicals. Cash tax: FY0 cash taxes paid 16,985m = 25.8% of pre-tax income, current tax 22.6% (R&D credits on 7-9%-of-sales R&D), prior year 27.8%; path starts at 27% and drifts to 28%, below the ~30.6% statutory rate because the R&D credit is structural. Buybacks are funded (11.5bn FY0, 10.0bn prior) -- the flat count is paid for. The after-hours/regular-close flag: price is the 2026-10-30 TSE regular close, not volatile.

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities (cross-shareholdings and equity-method affiliates) at 85% of 35,355m carrying value
equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2026 tanshin balance sheet at 2026-06-30, line 317; income from these (dividend 1,578m, equity earnings 1,507m) is excluded from the OP-based flows
Q1 FY2026 tanshin balance sheet at 2026-06-30, line 367; flows are consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2021-FY2026, 209,121m -> 279,586m). Equity CAGR is not the right proxy here: a 75%+ total payout ratio returns most earnings, so book value compounds well below earnings.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.1% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 9.7% and revenue 6.0%: >30% divergence, explained by the 75% total payout (dividends 23.6bn + buybacks 11.5bn in FY0 against 49.7bn net income) rather than by any accounting break.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest income; SBC is nil throughout). The 3yr figure (41.7%) is distorted by the FY2023 base year (15.8bn reported FCF, a working-capital trough when inventories were built); the 5yr 7.4% is the representative figure and sits in line with revenue growth. EPS outgrows revenue because of the ~1.5%/yr buyback shrink and margin expansion from 24.6% to 28.3% EBITDA.

base.narrative: Y1 growth 6.0% sits between the maintained 3.6% guidance (289.7bn) and the ~7% run-rate implied by a Q1 that beat the outlook by 9.7bn; semis materials guided +18% on ~a fifth of sales adds ~3-4pp a year while agrochemicals and chemicals grow low-single digits, so group growth fades from 6% to 2% over ten years. EBITDA margin edges from 28.3% to 29.5% as semis mix rises against rising R&D fixed cost (the FY2022-26 band was 27.3-29.4%). Capex 7.5% of sales for three years for the Taiwan/China/Toyama build-out, then 7.0%; D&A rises toward 6.0%. Terminal cap 16x binds against Gordon at 7.5%/2.0%.

bull.narrative: AI-server and advanced-node demand keeps semis materials on management's +20%-or-more 2024-30 CAGR, the Q1 beat carries through so FY ending Mar-2027 lands ~+9% (well above the maintained guidance), RYZONIC (2027, ~15bn peak) and the 2028 insecticide launch on time, and the China BARC plant qualifies with local fabs. Margin reaches 31% on semis mix; the same WACC as base because risk is in the flows.

bear.narrative: The AI-capex cycle turns in the year ending Mar-2028: semis materials fall ~20% as fabs digest capacity, group revenue -5% with margin compressing to 25% on fixed R&D and under-absorbed new Taiwan/China capacity (the FY2023-24 analogue when EBITDA margin fell from 29.4% to 27.3% on a flat top line). Fluralaner/LEIMAY/GRACIA agrochemical sales keep sliding and a glyphosate-class regulatory tightening in Japan clips ROUNDUP; recovery is to 3% growth and a 27% margin, never the FY0 level. Terminal growth 1.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Semis materials (ARC/OptiStack, +18% guided) carry group growth of ~6% fading to 2%, with agrochemicals and chemicals growing low-single digits and Healthcare flat-to-down; EBITDA margin settles at 29.5%; capex stays elevated at 7.5% of sales through the overseas build-out then normalises to 7%. Value is a 16x-capped terminal on a mature ~15% owner-FCF margin.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI-node demand sustains the 20%+ semis CAGR, FY ending Mar-2027 beats guidance by the Q1 run-rate, RYZONIC and the new insecticide launch on schedule, and margins reach 31% on mix. The bull needs three independent things (semis cycle, ag-chem pipeline timing, China plant qualification) to go right.
scenario_narratives.bear: A semis downturn in year two (-5% group revenue, 25% margin), a continued slide in the legacy agrochemical franchise and tighter herbicide regulation leave the business growing ~3% at a 27% margin; the balance sheet (net debt 9bn, 70% equity ratio) means this is an earnings bear, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the Analysis flags semiconductor-cycle concentration as the single high-severity risk and Performance Materials now supplies nearly all incremental profit (all other segments grew profit ~2% in FY0), so a capex downturn is a live base-rate event, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires the AI-capex cycle, two agrochemical launches and an unproven China plant to all deliver, and the share price at ~21x earnings near its 52-week high already discounts much of that. No going-concern or single-regulator dependency, so bear is not pushed further.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Nissan Chemical is a high-ROE (20%) R&D-led specialty chemical whose earnings growth has concentrated into semiconductor process materials. The house value discounts consolidated operating cash flows at a JPY cost of capital with no SBC charge (none exists), charges the semis cycle through a 25%-weighted bear path rather than the discount rate, caps the terminal at 16x owner FCF, and adds the cross-shareholding portfolio at a haircut because its income is outside the flows. The flat share count ignores a funded ~1.5%/yr buyback, which is a deliberate conservatism.
key_risks_to_valuation: Semiconductor capex cycle: Performance Materials supplies nearly all incremental profit; a downturn is the bear path and the main reason the bear weight is 25%
Terminal cap and margin: the 16x cap binds in base, so the value is sensitive to whether a ~29.5% EBITDA margin on semis mix is sustainable against rising R&D fixed cost
Working-capital intensity: trade working capital is 55% of sales; if growth consumes the full structural share rather than the -20% modelled, FCF is 3-5bn/yr lower
Agrochemical regulation (glyphosate-class, ROUNDUP marketing rights in Japan) and the timing of RYZONIC (2027) and the 2028 insecticide
Yen: a stronger yen compresses overseas semis and agrochemical revenue; flows and discount rate are both JPY so the model carries no FX translation risk of its own
Cash tax: the 27-28% path relies on continuing R&D credits; reverting to the 30.6% statutory rate is worth ~4% of value
